_comment: The video shorts. tools/cut_shorts.py cuts video/<id>.mp4 from the recordings; tools/build.py lays out the carousel and the tutorial tiles. Times are seconds in the source recording. A cue draws a ring round box ([x, y, w, h] as % of the screen) at t seconds into the short, and its words a moment later, for d seconds; tap: true pulses the ring like a finger. draft: true keeps a short off the published site (build with --drafts to see it).

chapters.title: The Simple Reader
chapters.line: A page and a few big buttons. Nothing else.

chapters.title: The Margin
chapters.line: What a study Bible prints beside the text, one tap away.

chapters.title: Search
chapters.line: The verse you half-remember, from one word.

chapters.title: Ask – Tell Me More
chapters.line: Questions answered from trusted references, on the iPad itself.

chapters.title: Setting up
chapters.line: Two settings on the iPad that make the app sound and work its best.

shorts.title: Choosing a book and chapter
shorts.blurb: Tap the title to pick any book and chapter. The arrows step to the next or previous chapter.

cues.text: Pick a book, then a chapter

shorts.title: Making the words bigger
shorts.blurb: Size makes every word on the page larger, as large as you need.

cues.text: Tap the big A until it's comfortable

shorts.title: Hear it read aloud
shorts.blurb: Tap a verse, then Speak. Each word lights up as it's read. Tap the verse to pause, and again to carry on.

cues.text: Tap a verse to start there

shorts.title: Three ways to read
shorts.blurb: One setting decides how much is on the screen: Simple Reader, Reference Bible, or Ask – Tell Me More.

cues.text: Reference Bible adds Search and the Margin
Ask – Tell Me More adds Ask

shorts.title: The Margin
shorts.blurb: Beside the page: the people a verse names, its words in the Hebrew or Greek, and the verses that speak to it.

cues.text: Its words in the Hebrew or Greek
Small letters tie the verse to the margin
Cross-references, under the word they explain

shorts.title: A reference, and the way back
shorts.blurb: A tapped reference opens over the page. Go to takes you there, and a bookmark brings you back.

cues.text: It opens over the page; your place stays put

shorts.title: Over or beside the page
shorts.blurb: The Margin can sit beside the page or rise over it as a drawer you can raise and lower.

cues.text: Drag the bar to raise or lower it

shorts.title: Search for a word
shorts.blurb: Type a word or a phrase. Every verse that has it, and the word lit on the page.

cues.text: Lower the panel to see the page
It lights up on the page too

shorts.title: Narrowing it down
shorts.blurb: Whole Bible, Old Testament, New Testament, or just the book you're in. Tap a verse for its card.

cues.text: Narrow it to a testament or this book
Tap a verse for its card

shorts.title: Asking a question
shorts.blurb: Start from a suggestion, or ask in your own words, typed or spoken.

cues.text: Or ask in your own words

shorts.title: An answer from trusted references
shorts.blurb: Apple Intelligence reads the commentaries and dictionaries on this iPad and writes a short answer. Every point says where it came from.

cues.text: Reading the references, on this iPad

shorts.title: The references behind it
shorts.blurb: Under the answer, the references themselves, in their own words. A verse they mention opens as a card.

cues.text: The references, in their own words

shorts.title: Choosing what to see
shorts.blurb: Show every kind of reference, or just one: commentary, cross-references, the dictionaries.

shorts.title: Going to a verse, and back
shorts.blurb: Go to opens the verse in the Bible. The bookmark takes you back to where you were.

shorts.title: Settings
shorts.blurb: The reading profile, the voice, text size, the words of Christ in red, and which reference works Ask reads.

shorts.title: A better voice
shorts.blurb: Settings › Accessibility › Read & Speak › Voices: download a natural voice, then choose it in the app. A Siri voice is the most natural of all.

shorts.title: Turning on Apple Intelligence
shorts.blurb: Ask writes its answers with Apple Intelligence. Settings › Apple Intelligence & Siri, on an iPad that supports it.

carousel.title: Big buttons, nothing to set up
carousel.text: The page is the Bible. Above it, a few buttons, each larger than any you've pressed on an iPad, each labelled in words. No menus, no gestures to learn, nothing to confirm.

carousel.title: It reads to you
carousel.text: Tap Speak and the page is read aloud, every word lit as it's spoken. Pause and resume with one tap. Tap a verse and it picks up from there.

carousel.title: It listens to you
carousel.text: Every place you can type, you can talk instead. Say "Romans 8" and you're there. Say "who was Melchizedek" and you get the answer. Speech is recognised on the iPad itself.

carousel.title: It answers you
carousel.text: Ask about a name, a word, a passage, and you get the reference works' own words. On an iPad with Apple Intelligence, a short written answer to your question, every point cited.

carousel.title: A study Bible's margin
carousel.text: What is known about a verse sits beside the page: the people it names, its words in the Hebrew or Greek, the verses that speak to it, and commentary.

carousel.title: Ask Siri
carousel.text: "Open John 3:16 in Bible Reader." From the lock screen, from Shortcuts, from across the room. "Ask Bible Reader" and your question goes straight to Ask.
